metadata.framework: National Curriculum Framework (NCF) & State Board Syllabi

cbse.name: Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)
cbse.description: Nationwide curriculum aligned with NCERT textbooks and national entrance examinations.

chapters.name: Chemical Reactions and Equations
chapters.summary: How atoms rearrange to form new substances. Learn balancing equations, combination, decomposition, displacement, and redox reactions.
chapters.analogy: Like baking a cake: flour, sugar, and heat undergo a chemical transformation into something delicious that cannot be unbaked!
chapters.practice: Why do we apply paint on iron articles? (Answer: Paint creates a barrier preventing oxygen and moisture from causing rust/oxidation.)

chapters.name: Acids, Bases and Salts
chapters.summary: Understand pH scale, taste, litmus indicators, neutralization, and practical salts like baking soda, washing soda, and plaster of Paris.
chapters.analogy: Lemon juice (acid) feels sharp like sour candy, while soap (base) feels slippery. Together they cancel out to make neutral saltwater!
chapters.practice: Why does tooth decay start when the pH of the mouth is lower than 5.5? (Answer: Acid erodes tooth enamel made of calcium hydroxyapatite.)

chapters.name: Metals and Non-metals
chapters.summary: Physical and chemical properties, reactivity series, ionic bond formation, and extraction of metals from ores.
chapters.analogy: Metals are team players that happily share electrons, making them great wires and bells that ring!
chapters.practice: Why is sodium kept immersed in kerosene oil? (Answer: Sodium reacts vigorously with atmospheric moisture and oxygen, catching fire.)

chapters.name: Carbon and its Compounds
chapters.summary: Covalent bonding, tetravalency, catenation, homologous series, and functional groups (alcohols, aldehydes, carboxylic acids).
chapters.analogy: Carbon is the ultimate friendly LEGO brick: with 4 bonding arms, it can connect in chains and rings to build all living molecules!
chapters.practice: What is a homologous series? (Answer: A family of organic compounds having the same functional group and -CH2- difference between successive members.)

chapters.name: Life Processes
chapters.summary: The essential functions for survival: Nutrition (autotrophic & heterotrophic), Respiration, Transportation in humans and plants, and Excretion.
chapters.analogy: Your body is a bustling metropolis: blood is the delivery highway, lungs are the air filters, and kidneys are recycling centers!
chapters.practice: Why do herbivores have longer small intestines than carnivores? (Answer: Herbivores eat plant matter rich in cellulose, which takes longer to digest.)

chapters.name: Control and Coordination
chapters.summary: Nervous system, neurons, reflex arcs, human brain structure, and plant hormones (auxins, gibberellins, abscisic acid).
chapters.analogy: Neurons are like high-speed electrical telegraph cables carrying lightning-fast messages from your fingertips to your brain!
formulas: Reflex Arc: Receptor ➔ Sensory Neuron ➔ Spinal Cord ➔ Motor Neuron ➔ Effector
chapters.practice: What is the function of the myelin sheath in neurons? (Answer: It acts as an electrical insulator, speeding up nerve impulse transmission.)

chapters.name: How do Organisms Reproduce?
chapters.summary: Asexual reproduction (fission, budding, spore formation) vs. sexual reproduction in flowering plants and humans.
chapters.analogy: Reproduction is nature's way of passing down the sacred family recipe book so the species continues for generations!
chapters.practice: What is pollination? (Answer: The transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a flower.)

chapters.name: Heredity
chapters.summary: Mendelian genetics, dominant and recessive traits, monohybrid and dihybrid crosses, and sex determination in human babies.
chapters.analogy: Inheritance is like receiving a shuffled deck of cards from your mom and dad that decides your eye color and hair texture!
chapters.practice: Who determines the biological sex of a human child? (Answer: The father, because sperm carries either an X or a Y chromosome.)

chapters.name: Light – Reflection and Refraction
chapters.summary: Spherical mirrors, lenses, ray diagrams, mirror formula, magnification, and Snell's law of refraction.
chapters.analogy: A curved spoon reflects you upside-down or magnified, showing how bending light rays changes what your eyes perceive!
chapters.practice: Find the focal length of a lens of power -2.0 D. (Answer: f = 1 / P = 1 / -2.0 = -0.5 m, which is a concave lens.)

chapters.name: The Human Eye and the Colorful World
chapters.summary: Eye anatomy, defects of vision (myopia, hypermetropia, presbyopia), dispersion of light through a prism, and atmospheric refraction.
chapters.analogy: A glass prism is like a light filter that unweaves sunlight into its rainbow threads of red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and violet!
formulas: Angle of Deviation: D = i + e - A
chapters.practice: Why do stars twinkle while planets do not? (Answer: Stars are point-sized distant light sources affected by shifting atmospheric layers, while planets are closer extended sources.)

chapters.name: Electricity
chapters.summary: Electric current, potential difference, Ohm's law, resistance, series and parallel circuits, and Joule's heating effect.
chapters.analogy: Think of electricity like water flowing in pipes: voltage is water pressure, current is flow rate, and resistance is pipe thickness!
formulas: Power: P = V × I = I²R = V²/R
chapters.practice: Why are domestic electric appliances connected in parallel? (Answer: Each appliance gets full voltage, independent switches, and operates if one fails.)

chapters.name: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current
chapters.summary: Magnetic field lines, right-hand thumb rule, solenoid, Fleming's left-hand rule, electric motors, and domestic electric circuits.
chapters.analogy: Running electricity through a coiled wire turns it into an invisible magnet that can push, pull, and spin electric fans and motors!
formulas: Force on Conductor: F = B × I × L × sin(θ)
chapters.practice: What is the function of an earth wire in domestic circuits? (Answer: It provides a safe low-resistance path for leakage current to prevent electric shocks.)

chapters.name: Our Environment
chapters.summary: Ecosystems, food chains, 10% energy law, biological magnification, and ozone layer depletion by CFCs.
chapters.analogy: An ecosystem is a delicate web of life: sunlight feeds the grass, grass feeds the deer, and deer feed the lion!
formulas: Energy Transfer: Only 10% moves to next trophic level
chapters.practice: Why are food chains usually limited to 3-4 trophic levels? (Answer: Because 90% of energy is lost at each step, leaving very little energy for higher levels.)

chapters.name: Real Numbers
chapters.summary: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, proving irrationality of √2, √3, and decimal expansions of rational numbers.
chapters.analogy: Every composite number has a unique fingerprint made of prime numbers multiplied together!
keyConcepts: Prime Factorization Method for HCF & LCM
formulas: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b
chapters.practice: Prove that √5 is irrational using proof by contradiction.

chapters.name: Polynomials
chapters.summary: Geometrical meaning of zeroes, relationship between zeroes and coefficients of quadratic and cubic polynomials.
chapters.analogy: A polynomial is an algebraic recipe where the zeroes are the magic ingredient numbers that make the whole bowl equal zero!
chapters.practice: Find a quadratic polynomial whose zeroes are 2 and -3.

chapters.name: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
chapters.summary: Graphical method, substitution method, elimination method, and consistency conditions.
chapters.analogy: Two straight railway tracks: they can cross at one exact station (unique solution), run parallel forever (no solution), or lie right on top of each other (infinite solutions)!
chapters.practice: Solve for x and y: x + y = 14 and x - y = 4. (Answer: x = 9, y = 5).

chapters.name: Quadratic Equations
chapters.summary: Standard form, factorization, quadratic formula (Sridharacharya's rule), and nature of roots.
chapters.analogy: Throwing a basketball through the hoop makes a parabola arc. A quadratic equation solves when and where the ball touches the ground!
chapters.practice: Find the roots of 2x² - 7x + 3 = 0 using the quadratic formula.

chapters.name: Arithmetic Progressions
chapters.summary: Understanding sequence patterns, nth term of an AP, and sum of first n terms.
chapters.analogy: Climbing a staircase where every single step has the exact same height is an arithmetic progression!
chapters.practice: Find the 10th term of the AP: 2, 7, 12... (Answer: a = 2, d = 5, a10 = 2 + 9(5) = 47).

chapters.name: Triangles
chapters.summary: Similar figures, Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales theorem), and criteria for similarity of triangles (AAA, SSS, SAS).
chapters.analogy: A tiny photo on your phone and a huge poster print are similar figures: their shapes match perfectly even though their sizes differ!
formulas: If DE || BC in ΔABC, then AD/DB = AE/EC
chapters.practice: State and explain the Basic Proportionality Theorem.

chapters.name: Coordinate Geometry
chapters.summary: Distance formula, section formula for internal division, and mid-point formula.
chapters.analogy: Like a city map grid: using latitude and longitude coordinates, you can calculate the exact walking distance between any two locations!
chapters.practice: Find the distance between the points (2, 3) and (4, 1).

chapters.name: Introduction to Trigonometry
chapters.summary: Trigonometric ratios of acute angles, specific values (0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90°), and fundamental trigonometric identities.
chapters.analogy: Trigonometry lets you measure the height of a towering mountain or skyscraper without ever climbing to the top!
keyConcepts: sin, cos, tan, cosec, sec, cot
chapters.practice: If sin A = 3/5, find cos A and tan A.

chapters.name: Some Applications of Trigonometry
chapters.summary: Heights and distances, line of sight, angle of elevation, and angle of depression.
chapters.analogy: Looking up at a kite in the sky creates an angle of elevation with the ground. Trigonometry calculates the kite's exact flying altitude!
chapters.practice: A tower stands vertical on the ground. From a point 15m away, the angle of elevation of the top is 60°. Find its height.

chapters.name: Circles
chapters.summary: Tangent to a circle, number of tangents from a point, and theorems on tangent lengths.
chapters.analogy: A bicycle wheel rolling along flat pavement touches the road at one precise point of contact at each instant—a perfect tangent!
keyConcepts: Tangent is perpendicular to radius at point of contact
Lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal
formulas: PA = PB (Tangents from external point P)
chapters.practice: Prove that the tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal in length.

chapters.name: Areas Related to Circles
chapters.summary: Perimeter and area of a circle, area of sector, and area of segment of a circle.
chapters.analogy: Slicing a pizza creates sectors! The crust edge is arc length, and the cheesy slice is the sector area.
keyConcepts: Area of Segment = Sector Area - Triangle Area
chapters.practice: Find the area of a sector of a circle with radius 6 cm if angle of sector is 60°.

chapters.name: Surface Areas and Volumes
chapters.summary: Surface area and volume of combinations of solids: cubes, cuboids, spheres, hemispheres, cylinders, and cones.
chapters.analogy: An ice cream cone with a scoop of ice cream on top is a solid combination of a cone and a hemisphere!
formulas: Cone Curved Surface Area = πrl (where l = √(r² + h²))
chapters.practice: Two cubes each of volume 64 cm³ are joined end to end. Find the surface area of the resulting cuboid.

chapters.name: Statistics
chapters.summary: Mean, median, and mode of grouped data, and empirical relationship between the three central tendencies.
chapters.analogy: Statistics turns chaotic stacks of survey numbers into clear, simple trends that guide scientists and businesses!
chapters.practice: State the empirical relationship between mean, median, and mode.

chapters.name: Probability
chapters.summary: Classical definition of probability, elementary events, complementary events, impossible and sure events.
chapters.analogy: Flipping a fair coin has 2 equal possibilities: heads or tails. Probability gives exact mathematical values to uncertainty!
keyConcepts: P(E) = Number of Favourable Outcomes / Total Number of Outcomes
chapters.practice: A die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a prime number? (Answer: Prime numbers are 2, 3, 5 out of 6, so 3/6 = 1/2).

chapters.name: Crop Production and Management
chapters.summary: Agricultural practices: soil preparation, sowing, manures & fertilizers, irrigation, weed removal, harvesting, and granary storage.
chapters.analogy: Farming is like running a huge outdoor cafeteria for millions of people: every crop needs the right food, water, and care to thrive!
formulas: Kharif (Monsoon: Rice, Maize) | Rabi (Winter: Wheat, Gram)
chapters.practice: Why is drip irrigation considered the best technique for water conservation?

chapters.name: Microorganisms: Friend and Foe
chapters.summary: Bacteria, fungi, protozoa, and algae. Fermentation, antibiotics, vaccines, nitrogen cycle, and food preservation.
chapters.analogy: Microbes are like tiny secret workers: some bake fluffy bread and make tasty curd, while others are mischief-makers that spoil food!
chapters.practice: What is pasteurization and how does it prevent milk spoilage?

chapters.name: Coal and Petroleum
chapters.summary: Fossil fuels, carbonization, coal tar, coal gas, refining of crude oil, and conservation of natural resources.
chapters.analogy: Petroleum is ancient sunlight buried under prehistoric swamps for millions of years, condensed into liquid fuel!
formulas: Dead Vegetation + Heat + High Pressure (Millions of Years) ➔ Coal
chapters.practice: Why is petroleum called 'Black Gold'?

chapters.name: Combustion and Flame
chapters.summary: Conditions for burning, ignition temperature, types of combustion, fire control, and zones of a candle flame.
chapters.analogy: A campfire needs three friends to dance: fuel to burn, air to breathe, and enough heat to spark the party!
formulas: Combustion: Fuel + O2 ➔ CO2 + H2O + Heat + Light
chapters.practice: Why is the non-luminous outer zone of a flame the hottest zone?

chapters.name: Conservation of Plants and Animals
chapters.summary: Deforestation, biodiversity conservation, biosphere reserves, national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, and the Red Data Book.
chapters.analogy: A forest is like a living umbrella protecting soil, rain, and wild animals. Removing trees collapses the wildlife roof!
keyConcepts: Red Data Book of Endangered Species
formulas: Forest Coverage ➔ Soil Water Retention ➔ Climate Stability
chapters.practice: What is the difference between a Wildlife Sanctuary and a National Park?

chapters.name: Reproduction in Animals
chapters.summary: Sexual reproduction, male and female reproductive systems, fertilization (internal vs external), and metamorphosis in frogs.
chapters.analogy: A caterpillar turning into a butterfly or a tadpole growing legs is nature's miraculous transformation called metamorphosis!
chapters.practice: Explain the life cycle stages of a frog (Egg ➔ Tadpole ➔ Adult Frog).

chapters.name: Reaching the Age of Adolescence
chapters.summary: Puberty, physical and emotional changes, endocrine glands, hormones (testosterone, estrogen), and nutritional health.
chapters.analogy: Adolescence is like a bridge connecting childhood to adulthood, guided by hormonal chemical messengers!
chapters.practice: What role does the hormone thyroxine play, and why is iodine necessary in our diet?

chapters.name: Force and Pressure
chapters.summary: Push and pull forces, contact and non-contact forces (friction, gravity, electrostatic, magnetic), and atmospheric pressure.
chapters.analogy: Pressing a sharp thumbtack into a corkboard is easy because small tip area creates huge pressure with tiny force!
chapters.practice: Why do school bags have wide shoulder straps instead of thin strings?

chapters.name: Friction
chapters.summary: Cause of friction (surface irregularities), factors affecting friction, friction as a necessary evil, and rolling vs sliding friction.
chapters.analogy: Friction is like microscopic sandpaper teeth locking together: it wears out your sneakers, but without it you would slip and slide!
formulas: Rolling Friction < Sliding Friction < Static Friction
chapters.practice: Why are aeroplanes and fast bullet trains shaped like birds and fish?

chapters.name: Sound
chapters.summary: Sound produced by vibrating bodies, propagation through mediums, human ear mechanism, pitch, loudness, and noise pollution.
chapters.analogy: Pluck a stretched rubber band: as it vibrates back and forth, it pushes surrounding air molecules in sound waves straight to your ear!
keyConcepts: Human Hearing Range: 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz
formulas: Frequency = Number of Oscillations / Time (in seconds)
chapters.practice: Why can sound not travel through a vacuum like outer space?

chapters.name: Chemical Effects of Electric Current
chapters.summary: Conductors and insulators of liquids, electrolysis, electroplating, and practical industrial uses.
chapters.analogy: Electroplating is like giving cheap iron a shiny golden or chrome armor suit using the magic power of battery current!
chapters.practice: Why is water with a pinch of common salt a much better electrical conductor than pure distilled water?

chapters.name: Some Natural Phenomena
chapters.summary: Lightning discharge, transfer of charge, electroscopes, earthquakes, Richter scale, and safety precautions.
chapters.analogy: Lightning is like a giant cosmic static electric spark—just like when you rub your socks on a fuzzy carpet and touch a door knob!
formulas: Like charges repel; Unlike charges attract
chapters.practice: How does a lightning conductor protect tall buildings from lightning damage?

chapters.name: Light
chapters.summary: Laws of reflection, regular and diffuse reflection, multiple images in periscope and kaleidoscope, and human eye care.
chapters.analogy: Two parallel mirrors create a magical infinite reflection tunnel where your face repeats forever and ever!
keyConcepts: Angle of Incidence = Angle of Reflection
Reflected Ray, Incident Ray & Normal lie in same plane
chapters.practice: State the two fundamental laws of reflection.

chapters.name: Rational Numbers
chapters.summary: Properties of rational numbers: closure, commutativity, associativity, distributive property, and representation on number line.
chapters.analogy: Sharing 3 pizzas equally among 4 friends gives each person 3/4th of a pizza—a clean rational number!
keyConcepts: Distributive Property: a(b + c) = ab + ac
formulas: Multiplicative Inverse of a/b is b/a
chapters.practice: Find three rational numbers between 1/4 and 1/2.

chapters.name: Linear Equations in One Variable
chapters.summary: Solving linear equations with variables on one and both sides, and real-world word problems.
chapters.analogy: A balanced scale: whatever weight you add or take away from one side, you must do exactly the same to the other side!
keyConcepts: Setting up Equations from Word Problems
formulas: ax + b = c ➔ x = (c - b) / a
chapters.practice: Solve for x: 5x + 9 = 5 + 3x. (Answer: 2x = -4 ➔ x = -2).

chapters.name: Understanding Quadrilaterals
chapters.summary: Polygons, convex and concave polygons, interior and exterior angle sum properties, parallelograms, rhombuses, rectangles, and squares.
chapters.analogy: Quadrilaterals are a four-sided family: from the friendly parallelogram to the neat and orderly square where all angles are 90°!
keyConcepts: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal
chapters.practice: Find the measure of each exterior angle of a regular polygon with 9 sides. (Answer: 360° / 9 = 40°).

chapters.name: Data Handling
chapters.summary: Organizing data, frequency distribution tables, grouped frequency distribution, histograms, pie charts, and chance/probability.
chapters.analogy: A pie chart slices up your budget or sports scores just like a pizza so you can see the biggest slices in one glance!
keyConcepts: Central Angle of Pie Chart Sector
chapters.practice: Draw and interpret a simple pie chart showing a student's daily 24-hour activities.

chapters.name: Square and Square Roots
chapters.summary: Square numbers, properties of squares, Pythagorean triplets, finding square roots by prime factorization and long division.
chapters.analogy: A square tile grid with 7 rows and 7 columns contains exactly 49 square tiles (7² = 49)!
keyConcepts: Square Root by Long Division Method
chapters.practice: Find the square root of 729 using prime factorization. (Answer: 729 = 3⁶ ➔ √729 = 3³ = 27).

chapters.name: Cube and Cube Roots
chapters.summary: Cubes of numbers, cube patterns, prime factorization method for finding cube roots.
chapters.analogy: A Rubik's cube with 3 blocks on each edge contains 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 tiny mini-cubes (3³ = 27)!
formulas: Cube of an odd number is always odd
chapters.practice: Find the cube root of 1728 using prime factorization. (Answer: 12).

chapters.name: Comparing Quantities
chapters.summary: Ratios, percentages, discount, profit and loss, sales tax/GST, and compound interest calculated annually and semi-annually.
chapters.analogy: Simple interest is like earning rent once a year; compound interest is earning rent on your rent—making money multiply faster!
chapters.practice: Calculate compound interest on ₹10,000 for 2 years at 10% per annum compounded annually.

chapters.name: Algebraic Expressions and Identities
chapters.summary: Monomials, binomials, polynomials, addition and subtraction, multiplication of expressions, and standard algebraic identities.
chapters.analogy: Algebraic identities are mathematical shortcuts that let you square huge numbers in seconds without long multiplication!
chapters.practice: Expand using identities: (2x + 3y)².

chapters.name: Mensuration
chapters.summary: Area of trapezium, general quadrilateral, rhombus, surface area and volume of cuboid, cube, and right circular cylinder.
chapters.analogy: Finding the volume is seeing how many 1-litre bottles of water can fit inside a water tank!
keyConcepts: Area of Trapezium = ½ × (Sum of parallel sides) × height
Area of Rhombus = ½ × d1 × d2
chapters.practice: Find the volume of a cylinder whose base radius is 7 cm and height is 10 cm. (Answer: 1540 cm³).

chapters.name: Exponents and Powers
chapters.summary: Powers with negative exponents, laws of exponents, and expressing very large and small numbers in standard scientific notation.
chapters.analogy: Exponents are mathematical zoom lenses: writing 10¹² lets you count galaxies, and 10⁻⁹ lets you measure atoms without dozens of zeroes!
keyConcepts: Laws of Exponents (Multiplication, Division, Power of Power)
chapters.practice: Simplify: (2⁻¹ × 4⁻¹) ÷ 2⁻².

chapters.name: Direct and Inverse Proportions
chapters.summary: Direct proportion (as one increases, other increases), inverse proportion (as one increases, other decreases), and word problem applications.
chapters.analogy: More workers finish building a fence in fewer days (Inverse proportion), but buying more apples costs more money (Direct proportion)!
chapters.practice: If 15 workers can build a wall in 48 hours, how many workers will finish it in 30 hours?

chapters.name: Factorisation
chapters.summary: Common factor method, factorisation by grouping, using identities, splitting the middle term, and polynomial division.
chapters.analogy: Factorisation is unbaking an expression to see the prime ingredients that multiplied to create it!
keyConcepts: Splitting the Middle Term in ax² + bx + c
chapters.practice: Factorise: x² + 5x + 6. (Answer: (x + 2)(x + 3)).

chapters.name: Introduction to Graphs
chapters.summary: Line graphs, linear graphs, coordinates of points on a Cartesian plane, and reading independent/dependent variable relations.
chapters.analogy: A graph tells a visual story of a car's journey over time, turning rows of numbers into an easy mountain picture!
formulas: Slope = Change in y / Change in x
chapters.practice: Plot the points (1, 2), (2, 4), (3, 6) and verify if they form a straight line.

maharashtra.name: Maharashtra State Board (MSBSHSE)
maharashtra.description: Official Maharashtra Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board (SSC & HSC) curriculum with Balbharati textbooks.

chapters.name: Gravitation
chapters.summary: Kepler's laws of planetary motion, Newton's universal law of gravitation, acceleration due to gravity (g), free fall, and escape velocity.
chapters.analogy: Toss an apple in the air: Earth's gravitational pull gently pulls it back, exactly following Kepler's celestial dance!
chapters.practice: State Kepler's third law of planetary motion and write its mathematical equation (T² ∝ r³).

chapters.name: Periodic Classification of Elements
chapters.summary: Dobereiner's triads, Newlands' law of octaves, Mendeleev's periodic table, modern periodic law, and periodic trends in properties.
chapters.analogy: The periodic table organizes all 118 elemental building blocks like an orderly supermarket where every aisle has matching characteristics!
formulas: Periods (7 rows) | Groups (18 columns) | s, p, d, f blocks
chapters.practice: How does atomic radius vary down a group and across a period from left to right?

chapters.name: Chemical Reactions and Equations
chapters.summary: Rules of writing chemical equations, balancing, types of reactions (combination, decomposition, displacement, double displacement), oxidation and reduction.
chapters.analogy: When rust forms on iron, oxygen and water are gently stealing electrons over time in an oxidation reaction!
chapters.practice: What is an endothermic reaction? Give one example with chemical equation.

chapters.name: Effects of Electric Current
chapters.summary: Heating effect of electric current (Joule's law), electric power, magnetic effect of current, right-hand thumb rule, Fleming's rules, and electric motor/generator.
chapters.analogy: Electric current flowing through a coiled tungsten filament heats up so bright it glows—lighting up our cozy rooms!
keyConcepts: Joule's Law of Heating: H = I²Rt
chapters.practice: Explain the construction and working of an Electric Motor with a neat labeled diagram.

chapters.name: Heat
chapters.summary: Latent heat of fusion and vaporization, anomalous expansion of water, dew point, relative humidity, and specific heat capacity (principle of heat exchange).
chapters.analogy: In freezing winter, lakes freeze on top while fish swim safely below because water amazingly expands when it turns into cold ice!
keyConcepts: Hope's Apparatus for Anomalous Behavior of Water
chapters.practice: Why do aquatic animals survive in frozen lakes in cold countries during winter?

chapters.name: Refraction of Light
chapters.summary: Refraction of light rays passing through media, laws of refraction, refractive index, and twinkling of stars / mirage formation.
chapters.analogy: Put a pencil into a glass of water: it appears magically broken at the surface because light slows down in denser water!
chapters.practice: Explain the phenomenon of mirage in hot desert roads with ray diagrams.

chapters.name: Lenses
chapters.summary: Convex and concave lenses, sign convention, lens formula, magnification, human eye, defects of vision, and optical instruments.
chapters.analogy: Your eye lens is a natural autofocus camera, adjusting its thickness so you can read a book or admire distant stars!
formulas: Magnification: M = v / u = h2 / h1
chapters.practice: Distinguish between Myopia (near-sightedness) and Hypermetropia (far-sightedness).

chapters.name: Metallurgy
chapters.summary: Physical and chemical properties of metals and non-metals, reactivity series, extraction of metals (concentration of ores), refining, and corrosion.
chapters.analogy: Extracting pure aluminum from raw red bauxite rock is like sifting gold dust from muddy river sand!
keyConcepts: Concentration of Ores (Hydraulic, Magnetic, Froth Floatation)
chapters.practice: Explain the Froth Floatation process used for concentration of sulfide ores.

chapters.name: Carbon Compounds
chapters.summary: Covalent bonds in carbon, hydrocarbons, functional groups, nomenclature (IUPAC), chemical properties, polymers, and everyday macromolecules.
chapters.analogy: Carbon is the master architect of living nature: connecting in rings and chains to make everything from sweet honey to DNA!
chapters.practice: Give the IUPAC names for: CH3-CH2-OH and CH3-COOH.

chapters.name: Space Missions
chapters.summary: Need and importance of space missions, artificial satellites, satellite launch vehicles (PSLV), space research, and space debris management.
chapters.analogy: Satellites are our digital eyes in the sky, beaming GPS maps, weather storm warnings, and live cricket matches to our phones!
keyConcepts: Types of Orbits: Low Earth (LEO), Medium Earth (MEO), High Earth (GEO)
chapters.practice: What is a Geostationary Orbit (GEO) and why is it crucial for communication satellites?

chapters.name: Heredity and Evolution
chapters.summary: Transcription, translation, translocation, mutation, evidence of evolution (morphological, anatomical, vestigial, paleontological), and Darwin's theory.
chapters.analogy: Fossils are ancient stone photographs showing how whales evolved from four-legged land mammals millions of years ago!
chapters.practice: Define vestigial organs and name any two vestigial organs found in the human body.

chapters.name: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
chapters.summary: Cellular respiration (glycolysis, Krebs cycle, electron transport chain), energy from nutrients (carbs, proteins, fats), and cell division (mitosis & meiosis).
chapters.analogy: Mitosis is like a biological copy machine: one cell cleanly duplicates into two identical twin daughter cells to heal a scraped knee!
keyConcepts: Stages of Mitosis (Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase)
chapters.practice: With neat diagrams, explain the four stages of Mitosis cell division.

chapters.name: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
chapters.summary: Reproduction and types (asexual in unicellular & multicellular, sexual), human reproductive systems, menstrual cycle, modern assisted reproduction (IVF, surrogacy).
chapters.analogy: Reproduction ensures the continuity of life across generations, just like relay runners passing a golden baton in a race!
chapters.practice: What is IVF (In Vitro Fertilization) and when is it recommended for couples?

chapters.name: Environmental Management
chapters.summary: Ecosystem relationships, environmental conservation laws, biodiversity hotspots, sacred groves, and disaster management.
chapters.analogy: Sacred groves are ancient community-protected forests in Maharashtra where people conserve trees and rare herbs with spiritual respect!
keyConcepts: Role of Common Man in Conservation (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle)
formulas: Producer ➔ Primary Consumer ➔ Secondary Consumer ➔ Apex Predator
chapters.practice: What are Sacred Groves (Devrai) and what role do they play in biodiversity conservation?

chapters.name: Towards Green Energy
chapters.summary: Generation of electrical energy from thermal, nuclear, hydroelectric, wind, and solar sources. Merits and environmental impacts.
chapters.analogy: Solar panels drink clean sunlight like leaves, turning pure solar rays directly into electricity without smoke or carbon pollution!
formulas: Solar Energy ➔ Semiconductor ➔ DC Electrical Energy
chapters.practice: Why is energy generated from solar cells and wind turbines termed 'Green Energy'?

chapters.name: Animal Classification
chapters.summary: History of animal classification, traditional vs modern criteria (germ layers, coelom, symmetry, segmentation), and Phyla from Porifera to Chordata.
chapters.analogy: From sponge-like Porifera on ocean reefs to birds soaring in clouds, classification maps the family tree of all animal life on Earth!
keyConcepts: Subphylum Vertebrata (Pisces, Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves, Mammalia)
chapters.practice: Give four distinct characteristics of Phylum Arthropoda with examples.

chapters.name: Introduction to Microbiology
chapters.summary: Applied microbiology, industrial microbiology, dairy products, probiotic foods, microbial enzymes, bio-fuels, and microbial pollution control.
chapters.analogy: Microbes act as nature's microscopic bio-cleaners, chewing up toxic oil spills in the ocean and turning trash into clean biogas!
formulas: Lactose in Milk ➔ Lactic Acid by Lactobacillus
chapters.practice: What are probiotics and why are they recommended for digestive wellness?

chapters.name: Cell Biology and Biotechnology
chapters.summary: Cytology, stem cells and their therapeutic uses, organ donation, commercial applications of biotechnology (Bt cotton, golden rice), and DNA fingerprinting.
chapters.analogy: Stem cells are magical master cells that can transform into heart cells, brain neurons, or skin to heal damaged human organs!
keyConcepts: Genetically Modified Crops (Bt Cotton, Golden Rice)
formulas: Stem Cell ➔ Differentiation into specialized tissue
chapters.practice: Explain the therapeutic uses of Stem Cells in medical science.

chapters.name: Social Health
chapters.summary: Factors affecting social health, mental stress management, cybercrime and safe internet habits, and overcoming substance addiction.
chapters.analogy: Healthy hobbies like playing outdoor games, reading books, and laughing with real friends protect our minds from digital screen burnout!
formulas: Physical Health + Mental Balance + Social Harmony = Total Wellness
chapters.practice: What precautions should students take to stay safe from cybercrime and online scams?

chapters.name: Disaster Management
chapters.summary: Natural vs man-made disasters, disaster management cycle (pre-disaster preparedness & post-disaster rehabilitation), first aid, and mock drills.
chapters.analogy: Practicing a school fire drill or earthquake drop-cover-hold ensures your body knows exactly where to run safely when an emergency strikes!
keyConcepts: First Aid Procedures (ABC: Airway, Breathing, Circulation)
chapters.practice: What first-aid measures should be taken in case of burns and bleeding injuries?

chapters.name: Linear Equations in Two Variables
chapters.summary: Simultaneous linear equations, graphical method, Cramer's rule (determinants), and equations reducible to a pair of linear equations.
chapters.analogy: Cramer's rule is a mathematical secret decoder wheel using cross-multiplication to find unknown x and y in three clean steps!
formulas: Determinant D = |a b; c d| = ad - bc
chapters.practice: Solve using Cramer's rule: 3x - 4y = 10, 4x + 3y = 5.

chapters.name: Quadratic Equations
chapters.summary: Standard form ax² + bx + c = 0, solution by factorisation, completing square method, formula method, and relations between roots and coefficients.
chapters.analogy: Solving a quadratic equation tells you the two exact landing points of a kicked soccer ball!
formulas: Nature of roots based on Δ
chapters.practice: Find the discriminant of 2x² - 5x + 3 = 0 and determine the nature of its roots.

chapters.name: Arithmetic Progression
chapters.summary: Sequence, terms of an AP, nth term formula, sum of the first n terms of an AP, and practical daily life word problems.
chapters.analogy: Saving ₹10 on day 1, ₹20 on day 2, ₹30 on day 3 is an arithmetic progression that grows your piggy bank systematically!
chapters.practice: Find the sum of the first 20 natural numbers using the AP sum formula.

chapters.name: Financial Planning
chapters.summary: Goods and Services Tax (GST: CGST + SGST), tax invoice calculation, shares, face value, market value, brokerage, and mutual funds.
chapters.analogy: When you buy your favorite snack, the bill shows CGST (Central tax) and SGST (State tax) split equally in half!
formulas: GST = Taxable Value × Rate of GST
Dividend = Number of Shares × Face Value × Dividend%
chapters.practice: A watch is purchased for ₹1000 with 18% GST. Find CGST and SGST amounts.

chapters.name: Probability
chapters.summary: Random experiments, sample space (S), events (impossible, sure, mutually exclusive), and calculating probability P(A).
chapters.analogy: Tossing a coin or rolling a six-sided die lets us calculate the exact mathematical fairness of any game!
chapters.practice: Two coins are tossed simultaneously. Find the probability of getting at least one head.

chapters.name: Statistics
chapters.summary: Measures of central tendency: Mean (direct, assumed mean, step deviation methods), Mode, Median for grouped data, histograms, and pie diagrams.
chapters.analogy: A pie chart splits school survey results into delicious colored slices so anyone can understand big data at a glance!
keyConcepts: Drawing Frequency Polygons and Pie Charts
chapters.practice: State the formula for calculating the median of grouped data and explain each term.

chapters.name: Similarity
chapters.summary: Ratio of areas of two triangles, Basic Proportionality Theorem, converse of BPT, property of angle bisector, and areas of similar triangles.
chapters.analogy: A toy model of an electric train has the exact same proportions as the real full-sized train on the tracks!
keyConcepts: Theorem of Areas of Similar Triangles
chapters.practice: State and prove the Basic Proportionality Theorem.

chapters.name: Pythagoras Theorem
chapters.summary: Similarity of right-angled triangles, theorem of geometric mean, Pythagoras theorem proof, converse, and Apollonius theorem.
chapters.analogy: If you walk 3 km East and 4 km North, Pythagoras calculates that you are exactly 5 km from where you started!
keyConcepts: Geometric Mean Theorem: h² = p × q
chapters.practice: In ΔABC, ∠B = 90°, AB = 6 cm, BC = 8 cm. Find the length of hypotenuse AC.

chapters.name: Circle
chapters.summary: Circles passing through points, tangent theorem, converse, tangent segments theorem, touching circles, inscribed angle theorem, and cyclic quadrilaterals.
chapters.analogy: A circular clock face: hands make inscribed angles that measure half the arc they cut out on the rim!
keyConcepts: Opposite Angles of Cyclic Quadrilateral are Supplementary (180°)
chapters.practice: Prove that opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary.

chapters.name: Geometric Constructions
chapters.summary: Construction of similar triangles, and constructing tangents to a circle from a point on the circle and from an external point.
chapters.analogy: Using your compass and ruler like a master architect to sketch perfect tangent lines and proportional triangle drafts!
keyConcepts: Constructing Similar Triangle with Common Vertex
Tangent at a point using Center
formulas: Compass arc intersection ensures mathematical perpendicularity
chapters.practice: Describe the steps to construct tangents to a circle of radius 3.5 cm from an external point 7 cm from the center.

chapters.name: Coordinate Geometry
chapters.summary: Distance formula, section formula for internal division, coordinates of midpoint, coordinates of centroid of a triangle, and slope of a line.
chapters.analogy: Like GPS coordinates guiding airplanes safely to the airport runway by checking slope and distance!
keyConcepts: Slope m = tan θ = (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1)
chapters.practice: Find the slope of a line passing through points (2, 3) and (4, 7).

chapters.name: Trigonometry
chapters.summary: Trigonometric ratios, relationships, trigonometric identities, and word problems on heights and distances.
chapters.analogy: Trigonometry lets astronomers calculate the exact distance to the Moon using angle measurements!
keyConcepts: Trigonometric Ratios (sin, cos, tan, cosec, sec, cot)
chapters.practice: A kite is flying at a height of 60m above ground with string inclined at 60°. Find string length.

chapters.name: Mensuration
chapters.summary: Area of sector and segment of a circle, surface areas and volumes of cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone, sphere, hemisphere, and frustum of a cone.
chapters.analogy: A bucket is a frustum of a cone. Mensuration tells you exactly how many liters of water will fill it to the brim!
keyConcepts: Curved & Total Surface Area of Solids
chapters.practice: Find the volume of a sphere of radius 7 cm (Take π = 22/7).

gujarat.name: Gujarat Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board (GSEB)
gujarat.description: Official Gujarat State Board syllabus aligned with state textbooks and NCERT standards.

chapters.name: Chemical Reactions and Equations
chapters.summary: Types of chemical changes, word equations, balancing, and practical everyday oxidation effects.
chapters.analogy: Baking bread changes dough into sponge!
chapters.practice: Explain displacement reaction with an experiment.

chapters.name: Acids, Bases and Salts
chapters.summary: Indicators, pH scale in daily life, preparation of washing soda, baking soda, bleaching powder.
chapters.analogy: Toothpaste is a gentle base that neutralizes mouth acids!
chapters.practice: Why is plaster of Paris stored in moisture-proof containers?

chapters.name: Metals and Non-Metals
chapters.summary: Physical and chemical properties, reactivity series, metallurgy processes, and corrosion prevention.
chapters.analogy: Gold and platinum stay shiny forever because they refuse to react with air!
chapters.practice: Why are ionic compounds soluble in water?

chapters.name: Carbon and its Compounds
chapters.summary: Covalent bonds, versatility of carbon, soap action, and ethanol reactions.
chapters.analogy: Carbon forms the skeleton of all living cells!
chapters.practice: Explain the cleansing action of soap with micelle structure.

chapters.name: Life Processes
chapters.summary: Nutrition, cellular respiration, circulation of blood in human body, and excretion mechanism.
chapters.analogy: Blood is the river of life delivering oxygen to trillions of hungry cells!
chapters.practice: Draw a neat diagram of human heart and trace the path of oxygenated blood.

chapters.name: Real Numbers
chapters.summary: Euclid's division lemma, fundamental theorem of arithmetic, and rational number expansions.
chapters.analogy: Primes are the indivisible atoms of arithmetic!
chapters.practice: Find HCF and LCM of 12, 15 and 21.

chapters.name: Polynomials
chapters.summary: Zeroes of linear, quadratic, and cubic polynomials with graphical interpretations.
chapters.analogy: The x-intercepts of a curve are where the polynomial zeroes live!
chapters.practice: Find the zeroes of x² - 2x - 8.

chapters.name: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
chapters.summary: Graphical, substitution, elimination, and cross-multiplication methods.
chapters.analogy: Two flight paths intersecting at a single safe waypoint!
chapters.practice: Solve for x and y: 2x + 3y = 11, 2x - 4y = -24.

karnataka.name: Karnataka School Examination and Assessment Board (KSEAB)
karnataka.description: Official Karnataka Secondary Education curriculum based on DSERT guidelines.

chapters.name: Chemical Reactions and Equations
chapters.summary: Chemical transformations, balancing equations, combination, displacement, and redox reactions.
chapters.analogy: Rust on iron is slow combustion without a visible flame!
chapters.practice: Differentiate between displacement and double displacement reactions.

chapters.name: Acids, Bases and Salts
chapters.summary: pH scale, indicators, preparation of washing soda, baking soda, and plaster of Paris.
chapters.analogy: Acid neutralizes base just like cold ice cools hot tea!
chapters.practice: What is the role of tartaric acid in baking powder?

chapters.name: Electricity
chapters.summary: Electric potential, Ohm's law, factors affecting resistance, series/parallel combinations, and Joule's law.
chapters.analogy: Water flowing through wide pipes has low resistance and high current!
chapters.practice: State Ohm's law and write its mathematical formula.

chapters.name: Arithmetic Progressions
chapters.summary: Definition of AP, general term an, and sum of first n terms Sn.
chapters.analogy: A grandfather clock chiming once at 1, twice at 2, thrice at 3 is an AP!
chapters.practice: Find the 20th term of the AP: 4, 9, 14, 19...

chapters.name: Triangles
chapters.summary: Thales theorem (BPT), criteria for similarity of triangles, and Pythagoras theorem.
chapters.analogy: Pythagoras calculated the hypotenuse shortcut across right-angled fields!
formulas: AC² = AB² + BC² in right-angled ΔABC
chapters.practice: State Thales theorem with a neat diagram.

chapters.name: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
chapters.summary: Algebraic and graphical solutions, consistency, and unique solutions.
chapters.analogy: Two crossing lines share exactly one common intersection point!
chapters.practice: Solve: x + y = 10 and x - y = 2.

tamilnadu.name: Tamil Nadu State Board (TNBSE / DGE)
tamilnadu.source: Tamil Nadu Directorate of Government Examinations (dge.tn.gov.in)
tamilnadu.description: Official Samacheer Kalvi state curriculum by the Department of School Education, Tamil Nadu.

chapters.name: Laws of Motion
chapters.summary: Inertia, linear momentum, Newton's laws of motion, gravitation, and mass vs weight.
chapters.analogy: Seatbelts save lives by holding back inertia when brakes slam!
chapters.practice: State Newton's second law of motion and derive F = ma.

chapters.name: Optics
chapters.summary: Refraction of light, lenses, lens formula, human eye, and optical instruments.
chapters.analogy: A magnifying glass focuses sun rays to ignite paper!
chapters.practice: Distinguish between convex and concave lenses.

chapters.name: Atoms and Molecules
chapters.summary: Atomic mass, molecular mass, mole concept, Avogadro's number, and gas volumes.
chapters.analogy: A mole is like a baker's dozen, but with 6.023 × 10²³ tiny particles!
chapters.practice: Calculate the number of moles in 27g of Aluminum.

chapters.name: Relations and Functions
chapters.summary: Cartesian product, relations, representation of functions, and composition of functions.
chapters.analogy: A function is a magical machine: enter an input x, and it outputs a unique y!
chapters.practice: If A = {1, 3, 5} and B = {2, 3}, find A × B and B × A.

chapters.name: Numbers and Sequences
chapters.summary: Euclid's division lemma, Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, Arithmetic and Geometric Progressions.
chapters.analogy: Geometric progression doubles like multiplying bacteria: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32!
chapters.practice: Find the 8th term of the GP: 3, 6, 12, 24...

chapters.name: Algebra
chapters.summary: Simultaneous linear equations, quadratic equations, GCD & LCM of polynomials, and matrices.
chapters.analogy: Matrices organize data tables like spreadsheets to compute games and graphics!
chapters.practice: Solve x² - 3x - 10 = 0 by factorization.

up.name: Uttar Pradesh Board (UPMSP)
up.description: Official curriculum of Asia's largest state education board (UPMSP, Prayagraj).

chapters.name: Chemical Reactions and Equations (रासायनिक अभिक्रियाएं एवं समीकरण)
chapters.summary: Balancing equations, types of reactions, oxidation-reduction, and corrosion.
chapters.analogy: लोहे पर जंग लगना ऑक्सीकरण का एक दैनिक उदाहरण है!
chapters.practice: रासायनिक समीकरण को संतुलित करना क्यों आवश्यक है?

chapters.name: Acids, Bases and Salts (अम्ल, क्षारक एवं लवण)
chapters.summary: pH value, litmus test, bleaching powder, and plaster of paris preparation.
chapters.analogy: नींबू का रस खट्टा अम्ल है और बेकिंग सोडा क्षारक है!
chapters.practice: pH पैमाना क्या है? मानव शरीर के लिए सामान्य pH परास लिखिए।

chapters.name: Light – Reflection and Refraction (प्रकाश – परावर्तन तथा अपवर्तन)
chapters.summary: Mirror and lens formula, reflection from spherical surfaces, and refraction.
chapters.analogy: समतल दर्पण में बनने वाला प्रतिबिंब आभासी और सीधा होता है!
chapters.practice: प्रकाश के परावर्तन के नियमों को चित्र सहित समझाइए।

chapters.name: Real Numbers (वास्तविक संख्याएं)
chapters.summary: Euclid division algorithm, prime factorization, and irrationality proofs.
chapters.analogy: अभाज्य संख्याएं गणित की मूल ईंटें हैं!
chapters.practice: सिद्ध कीजिए कि √3 एक अपरिमेय संख्या है।

chapters.name: Polynomials (बहुपद)
chapters.summary: Zeroes of quadratic polynomials and verification of coefficients.
chapters.analogy: बहुपद के शून्यक वह संख्याएं हैं जो समीकरण को शून्य बनाती हैं!
chapters.practice: द्विघात बहुपद x² + 7x + 10 के शून्यक ज्ञात कीजिए।

chapters.name: Quadratic Equations (द्विघात समीकरण)
chapters.summary: Factorization, quadratic formula, and discriminant nature of roots.
chapters.analogy: क्रिकेट गेंद का परवलयाकार मार्ग द्विघात समीकरण द्वारा दर्शाया जाता है!
chapters.practice: समीकरण 2x² - 4x + 3 = 0 का विविक्तकर ज्ञात कीजिए।

rajasthan.name: Board of Secondary Education Rajasthan (RBSE / BSER)
rajasthan.source: Board of Secondary Education Rajasthan, Ajmer (rajeduboard.rajasthan.gov.in)
rajasthan.description: Official Rajasthan Board curriculum prescribed by RBSE Ajmer for secondary and higher secondary schools.

chapters.name: Chemical Reactions and Equations (रासायनिक अभिक्रियाएँ एवं समीकरण)
chapters.summary: Balanced equations, combination, decomposition, displacement, and rancidity/oxidation in daily life.
chapters.analogy: Baking soda and vinegar fizzing with carbon dioxide bubbles!
chapters.practice: संतुलित रासायनिक समीकरण किसे कहते हैं? एक उदाहरण दीजिए।

chapters.name: Acids, Bases and Salts (अम्ल, क्षारक एवं लवण)
chapters.summary: Indicators, pH scale, washing soda, bleaching powder, and plaster of Paris.
chapters.analogy: Antacid tablets neutralizing excess hydrochloric acid in stomach!
chapters.practice: विरंजक चूर्ण (Bleaching Powder) का रासायनिक नाम एवं सूत्र लिखिए।

chapters.name: Life Processes (जैव प्रक्रम)
chapters.summary: Human digestive system, cellular respiration, blood circulatory system, and kidney excretion.
chapters.analogy: The circulatory system is a continuous highway delivering oxygen to every organ!
chapters.practice: नेफ्रॉन का नामांकित चित्र बनाकर उसके मुख्य कार्य बताइए।

chapters.name: Real Numbers (वास्तविक संख्याएँ)
chapters.summary: Euclidean algorithm, prime factorization, and proving irrationality of √5.
chapters.analogy: Prime numbers build all composite numbers like atomic blocks!
chapters.practice: सिद्ध कीजिए कि √5 एक अपरिमेय संख्या है।

chapters.name: Pair of Linear Equations (दो चरों वाले रैखिक समीकरण युग्म)
chapters.summary: Graphical and algebraic methods: elimination, substitution.
chapters.analogy: Finding the exact point on a map where two roads meet!
chapters.practice: रैखिक समीकरण युग्म 2x + y = 6 और 2x - y = 2 को हल कीजिए।

chapters.name: Introduction to Trigonometry (त्रिकोणमिति का परिचय)
chapters.summary: Trigonometric ratios (sin, cos, tan), specific angles 30°, 45°, 60°, and identities.
chapters.analogy: Surveyors measuring tall mountain peaks without climbing them!
formulas: tan θ = sin θ / cos θ
chapters.practice: यदि sin A = 3/4 है, तो cos A और tan A का मान ज्ञात कीजिए।

westbengal.name: West Bengal Board of Secondary Education (WBBSE / WBCHSE)
westbengal.source: West Bengal Board of Secondary Education (wbbse.wb.gov.in) & WBCHSE
westbengal.description: Official Madhyamik (Class 10) and Uchha Madhyamik (Class 12) curricula of West Bengal.

chapters.name: Concerns about Our Environment (পরিবেশের জন্য ভাবনা)
chapters.summary: Layers of atmosphere, ozone layer depletion, greenhouse effect, and sustainable energy sources.
chapters.analogy: The ozone layer is Earth's natural sunglasses blocking harsh ultraviolet rays!
chapters.practice: What causes the depletion of the ozone layer in the stratosphere?

chapters.name: Behavior of Gases (গ্যাসের আচরণ)
chapters.summary: Boyle's law, Charles's law, Avogadro's law, and the ideal gas equation PV = nRT.
chapters.analogy: Hot air balloons rise high because heating expands gas and lowers its density!
chapters.practice: State Boyle's Law and express it mathematically.

chapters.name: Periodic Table & Chemical Properties (পর্যায় সারণি)
chapters.summary: Mendeleev's periodic law, Modern periodic table, periodic trends (atomic radius, ionization energy, electronegativity).
chapters.analogy: Periodic table is the ultimate chemical filing cabinet where elements with similar personalities sit in the same column!
chapters.practice: How does atomic radius change along a period and down a group?

chapters.name: Control and Coordination in Living Organisms (জীবজগতে নিয়ন্ত্রণ ও সমন্বয়)
chapters.summary: Plant movements (tropic, nastic), plant hormones (Auxin, Cytokinin), human nervous system, and reflex actions.
chapters.analogy: Touch-me-not plant folds its delicate leaves when tapped due to sudden turgor pressure changes!
formulas: Stimulus ➔ Receptor ➔ Nerve ➔ Brain/Spinal Cord ➔ Effector
chapters.practice: Distinguish between tropic movement and nastic movement in plants.

chapters.name: Continuity of Life (জীবনের ধারাবাহিকতা)
chapters.summary: Chromosome structure, DNA & RNA, cell cycle, mitosis, meiosis, and reproduction.
chapters.analogy: Chromosomes are condensed biological library volumes containing all hereditary genes!
chapters.practice: Why is Meiosis called reductional division?

chapters.name: Quadratic Equations in One Variable (একচলবিশিষ্ট দ্বিঘাত সমীকরণ)
chapters.summary: Standard form ax² + bx + c = 0, factorization, Sridhar Acharya's formula, and nature of roots.
chapters.analogy: Sridhar Acharya was an ancient Indian mathematician who gave the universal quadratic formula!
chapters.practice: Find the roots of x² - 5x + 6 = 0 using Sridhar Acharya's formula.

chapters.name: Simple Interest (সরল সুদ)
chapters.summary: Principal, rate of interest, time, and simple interest calculations in banking.
chapters.analogy: Interest is the small rent paid for borrowing money from a bank!
chapters.practice: Calculate simple interest on ₹5000 at 6% per annum for 3 years.
